title: Aggregation Theory
equation: Aggregation Power = Demand Owned ÷ Supply Owned
hook: If a marketplace owns your customers, you're basically renting your business.
statement: Online, the power goes to whoever owns the customer relationship, not whoever makes the product.
explainer: Big platforms win by owning the customer, then making suppliers compete for access. If all your sales run through someone else's platform, they set the rules and can squeeze your margin.
sop: Map whether you mainly own customers or mainly own product.
Rate Demand Owned and Supply Owned from 1 to 10.
List the platforms you depend on for customers.
Build a direct channel, like an email list or your own site.
Cut dependence on any platform that could squeeze you.
equation_example: Demand Owned 8 ÷ Supply Owned 2 = 4. Above 1 means you own the customer and suppliers compete for you. Below 1 means you're the supplier fighting for access to someone else's customers.
question: Write down what percent of your sales come through a platform you don't control.
closing_statement: Owning the relationship beats owning the product.
caption:
Principle Nº 346: Aggregation Theory

If a marketplace owns your customers, you're basically renting your business.

Online, the power goes to whoever owns the customer relationship, not whoever makes the product.

Your turn: Write down what percent of your sales come through a platform you don't control.
